## Start with one representative question

[S01-Q041](#S01-Q041)

<p>When would you choose Factory, Strategy or Template Method for a changing requirement? Explain what varies and compare your choice with a simpler design.</p>

## One group objective and observable capabilities

<p>Select a creation or behavior boundary that makes an expected variation manageable.</p>

<ul>
<li>Identify what varies in construction, behavior or workflow.</li>
<li>Compare Factory, Strategy and Template Method with a simple implementation.</li>
<li>Explain extension, dependency and testing costs.</li>
</ul>

**Prerequisites**

- [Dependency contracts and lifetime ownership](dotnet-di-solid.md)

<p>Start with the change you need to support, then locate the part that varies. This makes the comparison between creation, replaceable behavior and a shared workflow a design decision rather than a vocabulary exercise.</p>

### S01-Q041 · Trade-offs

<p>When would you choose Factory, Strategy or Template Method for a changing requirement? Explain what varies and compare your choice with a simpler design.</p>

**Source:** [S01-Q041](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q041)

<details markdown="1" class="question-original">
<summary>Original source wording and provenance</summary>

**[S01-Q041](../../sources/01-csharp-dotnet.md#q041)**

<div lang="en" markdown="1">

> When would you use Factory, Strategy, or Template Method?

</div>

</details>

<details markdown="1" class="question-guidance">
<summary>What the question asks and how to assess an attempt</summary>

**What to clarify**

<p>Separate object creation, interchangeable behavior and a reusable workflow. Use the pattern only when its boundary matches the actual variation.</p>

**Inferred assessment intent**

<p>Select a pattern from change pressure rather than name recognition.</p>

**Scope and important assumptions**

<p>Use one hypothetical scenario with a defined extension requirement; do not claim experience or performance benefits from using the pattern alone.</p>

**Observable signs of a strong senior answer**

<ul>
<li>Traces how a new variant enters the design and what existing code changes.</li>
<li>Explains dependency, testing and complexity consequences relative to a simple alternative.</li>
</ul>

**Misconceptions and shallow answers to watch for**

<ul>
<li>Presenting all three as interchangeable ways to remove an if statement.</li>
</ul>

**Related follow-ups — agent-added**

<ul>
<li>What requirement would make inheritance less suitable than composition in your example?</li>
</ul>

</details>

## Combined production exercise — agent-added

<p>A hypothetical import feature gains a new format and different validation behavior. State the variation, sketch a minimal design, then compare one candidate pattern. Show what adding another format changes and how existing behavior stays covered by tests; name a condition favoring the simpler option.</p>

## Short rubric — use only with an actual attempt

**Basic answer**

<p>Describes each candidate’s intended role and selects one matching the variation.</p>

**Senior answer**

<p>Defends the boundary and its testing and complexity costs against a credible simpler option.</p>

**Still needs evidence**

<p>A pattern diagram without an actual change trace does not demonstrate maintainability.</p>
